angle: A workbench that opens on the text, not a dashboard that opens on the job. The pastor's deliverable is today's chapter already readable, and one place for what he lifts out of it; every source names itself, and the assistant never writes.
thesis: A pastor opens Daily Word in the gap between two other things. Today he lands on a photo carousel with a Read button, and the first card above his reading is one that leaves the app (HomeScreen.tsx:2106 renders the Preach card above the hero; expandedPassages starts empty at HomeScreen.tsx:222). So the screen asks him to work before it gives him anything. The fix is not more features — the pastor path already has the deepest toolset in the app. It is order and honesty: put the chapter on the screen already open and credit-free, put the collector for what he pulls out of it directly underneath, move the leave-the-app card below both, and make every commentary, cross-reference and AI answer name its own source. That is the research's ranked list for this persona in the order it ranks it — framing first, trust panel second, time-saved third — and it is the smallest change that respects the one thing this persona has that the others do not: he is not reading for himself alone, and the app currently gives him a bag to file into (dw_sermon_prep) with no surface in the app that can open it.
principles: The deliverable is the chapter. It is on screen when he arrives, in paper mode, credit-free — never behind a picture and a tap.
Nothing is asked that the app already knows. It knows the day, the chapter, the campus, whether he is signed in, what he filed, whether he read yesterday.
The assistant finds and shows sources. It never authors. Every study result carries its source and licence on the same screen it appears on.
Real numbers or no numbers. No seeded counts, no invented minutes — a lesson this app already learned once and half-forgot (the fabricated counter still lives in src/sections/CampusCountSection.tsx).
One collector, not a second workspace. What he highlights goes to one bag with a visible receipt and one door out.
Richer, not stripped. Every removal here is a reordering or a fabrication; the reading gets longer and warmer, not shorter.
No streak talk at a man who is 38% likely to have considered quitting this year. Count the habit, name the return, never the reset.
Every change to the opening screen ships behind a preview link he approves first.

journey.day0: He picks Leader / Pastor in the one sheet ("Where are you today?"), or is already stamped by staff sign-in. The sheet saves and opens Home in the same tap; if he is signed in as staff, the sheet shows the note and "Sign out of pastor account" — no lock glyph, and he can still choose any path. He lands on Home with 1 Peter 5 already readable (PASTOR_CHAPTERS rotation, src/data/pastor.ts), the greeting reading "This is your time — not ministry, just you and God", and nothing asking him for anything. No wizard, no plan funnel, no email ask.
journey.first_session: He reads. If a line lands, he highlights it and taps "To sermon" (already live, HighlightToolbar.tsx:45). Directly under the reading a For Sunday card now shows what he just filed — the first thing in the app that has ever shown him that bag. He taps Mark as read once; DoneCelebration is calm. Only after that does a single line offer a plan. Commentary is open below, each entry naming its source. Median session is under four minutes and he leaves with something filed.
journey.return_visit: Same shape, next chapter. The reading is open again on arrival. The For Sunday card carries yesterday's items forward and now names his focus ("Philippians · week 2") because he typed it once. "Read what I'm preaching" has put Philippians into today's reading, so the chapter he opens is the chapter he is working on — the single self-serve lever that makes this app his and needs no developer.
journey.week2: The bag has eight or nine pieces. The Preach card, now below the reading, hands the bag to Pastors Sermon Prep. Bible AI's four pastor prompts get used against real filed material rather than an empty bag, and every answer ends with its sources. On Monday a week card shows two true numbers — days read, pieces filed — which is the honest form of the research's "show time saved". Campus Overview shows real campus numbers if he signed in, and the code prompt if not.
journey.missed_day: Nothing changes on the screen except one word in the greeting: "Good to have you back." No day number, no reset, no red. The streak freeze already bridges a single day (streak.ts:65-66) and the reading is open as always. If he missed a whole week, the Monday week card does not render at all rather than reporting a zero.
journey.seasonal: Sunday is the one day the app stops asking anything of him: no week card (it moves to Monday for this persona), no plan nudge, and the reading stays. The week card and the plan offer resume Monday. Church-wide seasonal reads reach him as a congregation member would see them, through Plans — no leaders featured row, which Ashley rejected.

comfort_access: The research's second build priority is one persistent comfort tap from every path, and this persona is where the case is strongest: Barna reports 65% of pastors report loneliness, up from 42% in 2015, and 38% considered quitting in the past year. But a pastor will not tap a card labelled "I need comfort" on his own home screen, and switching his saved path would be wrong. So comfort reaches him through the one card already addressed to him and not to his church: "Between You & God" gets a third action, "Just scripture today". Tapping it swaps the reading panel above to the comfort chapter rotation, hides Mark as read and the streak chip for that session, and writes nothing — no dw_setup change, no source stamp, no path arrival strip. There is no graduation prompt, no next-day check-in, and no follow-up of any kind; that pattern is removed for good and must never come back. If the crisis-line safety flow is built for the comfort path, it applies here identically, with the region-correct number for the campus on his profile.
reminders: One a day, at the hour he actually opens, in neutral words. The machinery exists — hourly cron, per-subscriber preferred_hour, a two-hour catch-up window, a once-per-local-day ledger — and it is currently a fixed hour he sets by hand in Settings. The research is explicit that guilt-framed streak reminders drive opt-out and uninstall, and that behaviour-inferred timing is the pattern that works. So: after five to seven sessions, infer his median open hour and offer to move the reminder there once ("You usually open this around 6:40. Want the reminder then?"), then leave it alone. The push copy is a passage line, never a streak line — the templates in push-send.js are already scripture snippets and must stay that way for this persona. Never send on the streak's behalf, never say "your streak is about to end", and never send twice. Push cannot be verified on a deploy preview — pushSupported() allowlists prod and localhost only — so any reminder change is verified on futuresdailyword.com after merge, not on the preview link Ashley approves.

D1 / D7 / D30 by path, session length, and reminder opt-out rate — the research's first build, and the only place these numbers can ever come from. One dw_events table, one nightly rollup, persona as a dimension.

Framing A/B: the ai_pastor_framing line on versus off, measured on pastor AI prompt use and on weekly return. The research names this as the highest-leverage copy change in the app and asks for it to be tested directly rather than assumed.
Every new event string must be added to the TRACKED_EVENTS allowlist in src/utils/analytics.ts:24-31 or it is silently dropped.
self_serve_levers: Preaching focus — editable in place on the For Sunday card, writes dw_sermon_prep_focus, syncs, and seeds the AI outline prompt. Today it is only capturable inside step 13 of a wizard he may never open.

"Read what I'm preaching" — turns that focus into a reading slot (dw_reading_slots) so Daily Word reads the book he is preaching. This is the single most valuable self-serve lever for a campus pastor: it changes what the app shows him every morning, with no developer and no new plan id (which would need rewiring in four places).
Chapters per day — dw_chapters_per_day, already user-set, governs how much of the plan and slots the hero shows.
The prep bag itself — file and remove items, cap 40, works offline.
Path — the swatch in the Home header opens the sheet from any screen; a signed-in pastor can pick any path as a real choice and sign out of the pastor account from inside the sheet.
Campus — the location chip in the Home header applies on tap, no Settings trip. Adding a NEW campus still needs a developer (CAMPUSES in src/data/tokens.ts).
Congregation for sermon notes — Futures USA / Futures Australia / Futuros, chosen from the card, remembered.
Pastor code — staff sign-in provisions it automatically and Campus Overview picks it up without a remount; hand-entry is the fallback and is deliberately not persisted as a sign-in.
Translation, scripture font size, reminder hour, push on/off, language — all in Settings today.
Study sources list — entirely data-driven from the study_* tables; adding or removing a source updates the attribution card with no code change.

What a campus pastor still CANNOT change without a developer, and should be told plainly: the 15 reflection prompts (persona-config.ts:468-482), the 30-chapter pastor rotation (src/data/pastor.ts), the wizard's plan recommendations (PastorStudyOnboarding.tsx:148-247), push wording (netlify/functions/push-send.js), the Preach destination URL (HomeScreen.tsx:74), and the sermon frameworks — which are 4D and H.E.A.T. only, both sourced to Multiply or Die, and a third must never be invented.

evidence.source: Research persona 5: ~70% of SBC pastors spend 8+ hours a week on sermon prep, 21% spend 15+ — Sunday is the delivery day. The card is currently Sundays-only at HomeScreen.tsx:109. This is a per-persona day change, not the weekly-review-for-all that Ashley rejected.

evidence.move: Return language after a missed stretch instead of a day count
evidence.source: Research cross-cutting finding 6: "Streaks work until they shame… guilt-framed streak reminders drive notification opt-out and uninstall", with streak repair rather than a hard reset. Persona 5: Barna, 38% of pastors considered quitting in the past year.

evidence.move: A comfort door inside Between You & God, with no graduation prompt
evidence.source: Research build priority 2, "Comfort from everywhere", plus persona 5's 65% pastor loneliness (up from 42% in 2015). The no-graduation constraint is a hard ruling: "Comfort's 'Feeling Stronger?' graduation prompt is removed for good — never re-add."

evidence.move: Gate the plan wizard behind the first completed reading
evidence.source: Research cross-cutting finding 2 (zero-decision first move) and persona 5's time-relief need. Live: PastorStudyOnboarding renders a full card on first Home load whenever no plan exists (PastorStudyOnboarding.tsx:21-30).

evidence.move: Neutralise the fabricated campus counter without deleting the file
evidence.source: src/sections/CampusCountSection.tsx computes a reader count from a seed on the campus id — the exact pattern removed from Campus Overview. It is currently exported but rendered nowhere, and 'campus_count' is still in pastor_leader's sectionOrder (persona-config.ts:446). The file itself must survive because "If HomeScreen is ever re-extracted/retired, the ten src/sections/* files and their tests must come back with it."

evidence.move: Ship the whole thing behind a preview link
evidence.source: Ruling: never re-merge or ship a big IA reshape of the opening screen without Ashley previewing and explicitly approving it first; and a PR may sit open awaiting his deploy-preview look and must not be merged without his word.

open_decisions: Does the For Sunday card stay a receipt and a door, or does it become the in-app workspace? src/screens/PreachScreen.tsx and its four components (PrepSheet, OutlineBuilder, PublishSermon, SermonArchive) are built and unit-tested but unmounted by your 9 Sep call. This design keeps them unmounted and keeps the handoff out to Pastors Sermon Prep. Reversing that is a one-line routing change plus the tab wiring, and only you can decide whether preaching lives inside Daily Word or beside it.
Book cards on the pastor Home — demote to the bottom, as designed here, or drop them for this persona entirely. They are your books, so this is your call, not the evidence's.

Is "You read 4 days last week, 7 pieces filed" the version of "time saved" you want, or do you want a minutes figure? A minutes figure cannot be measured honestly today and would be the same class of number as the seeded campus counts we removed.

The pastor tier price, and whether it is flat. The research names the Logos subscription backlash as a live reason pastors abandon tools; nothing in Daily Word prices anything today, so this is unbuilt rather than wrong.
Once "Read what I'm preaching" exists, what should a pastor with no plan see by default — the PASTOR_CHAPTERS rotation, or his preaching book from the first day he names it?
Whether the crisis-line safety flow (region-correct numbers per congregation) applies on this path as well as comfort, and who at each campus receives a prayer request raised from it.
risks: This reshapes the opening screen, which is the exact class of change you reverted once as "completely stripped". The difference is direction: this adds the chapter text to the first screen and removes nothing but a photo plate and a card's position. It still ships behind a preview link and must not merge without your word.

The arrival seed is the highest-risk line of code here. If it routes through handleRead it will credit a plan day and fire daily_reading on every Home mount for four personas — silently inflating completion and advancing plans nobody read. The check has to be a test that asserts the seed path never reaches markPlanDayComplete, recordStreakToday or dw_reading_done.

Seeding a chapter open means a passage fetch on every Home mount. It must reuse the existing passage cache and not refetch per mount, or a pastor on a train pays for a chapter he already has. ESV needs the Netlify function, so this cannot be verified in plain vite dev — use the dw-dev preview server or the deploy preview.

home-pastor-floor.test.ts pins several things this design touches: the hero fallback to PASTOR_CHAPTERS, the exact preach_card_sub copy, the deep-link return-before-chooser behaviour, and that App.tsx never imports PreachScreen. Moving the card must leave all four assertions true.

BibleAI.pastor.test.tsx pins the four prompt labels, their order, and the outline message format. The framing line goes above the block; touching the labels breaks the test and, more importantly, breaks copy you already approved.

dw_sermon_prep rides the misc bag with whole-value replace. Removing an item rewrites the array, which is correct under newest-wins — but the For Sunday card must merge into what is currently in localStorage and touch only its own fields, never rebuild the record from React state, or a second device's filed items are lost.
Campus Overview and the sources line are both network. If either shows an error rather than degrading, an offline pastor sees two failures on a screen that should just be a chapter.

'campus_count' sitting in pastor_leader's sectionOrder is a live landmine: the day sectionOrder is wired to the src/sections/* components, CampusCountSection resurrects seeded numbers for pastors. Gut the fabrication now even though nothing renders it.
No /books or /bible JSON changes here, so no service-worker cache work is required. If that changes, /books/* must stay network-first and CACHE_NAME, STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION bump together.
Reminder behaviour cannot be verified on the preview link — pushSupported() allowlists prod and localhost only. Verify reminders on futuresdailyword.com after merge.
